sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球海事商船注册旗国、借鉴特拉华州公司法的非公开发行实体

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, Title 51, Marshall Islands Revised Statutes (as amended), §§ 5, 7, 8, 21, 34, 35, 36, 43, 44 and 45 (authorized capital, articles of incorporation, registered office and agent, directors, officers, shares)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Republic of the Marshall Islands
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Marshall Islands Business Corporation Form 1)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; authorized capital may be issued in whole or part. No escrow account or capital deposit required for non-resident business corporations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Corporation hereby accepts the offer to purchase 100 ordinary shares at US$1.00 each from the sole subscriber, and such shares are issued for cash to the extent of the paid-up amount recorded in the books; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Corporation shall be located at the address maintained by the registered agent in Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands, and the registered agent is approved; RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed officers of the Corporation with full authority to act on its behalf: President and Secretary, each to serve until successors are duly elected; RESOLVED, that the President and Secretary are authorized to execute banking documents, charter agreements, and registry filings necessary to transact the Corporation’s maritime business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Majuro, Republic of the Marshall Islands (online portal via RMI Commercial Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search in the RMI corporate registry. If available, submit a Name Reservation Request with the desired corporate name ending with 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Limited' or an approved abbreviation. Payment of the reservation fee is required online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved for another entity, submit an alternate name within two business days; request administrative review by the Registrar with supporting evidence of distinctive use.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel or accredited corporate services provider; final filing with Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation containing corporate name, registered office and registered agent address, purpose clause (including ocean Ro-Ro vessel transportation), authorized capital structure, director names, and any permitted limitations on liability. The articles must be signed by the incorporator and notarized.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a defect notice, amend the articles and resubmit within the cure period (usually 10 business days) without additional fee for first resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Articles and Pay Filing Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Office of the Attorney General, Majuro
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized Articles of Incorporation and all required dossiers to the Registrar, either in person or through the RMI online filing system. Pay the official state filing fee (US$275 for non-resident business corporation). Retain the Registry receipt.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried due to incomplete information, provide the requested clarification or missing page within 5 business days. If no cure, re-file with payment of a 50% late-cure fee unless the error is solely attributable to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approved filings, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues a notarized Certificate of Incorporation. Verify the registration date, corporate number, and official seal. The Certificate authorizes the corporation to commence legal existence but not maritime operations until vessel licenses are obtained.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical or legal defect, file a Certificate of Correction with written minutes and pay a US$50 correction fee; Registry issues corrected certificate within 3 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent licensed under RMI Business Corporations Act; Registrar of Corporations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enter into a registered agent agreement with a licensed corporate service provider in Majuro. File the Registered Office / Agent Change form if not included in the Articles. The agent receives service of process and official mail.
required_dossiers: Form 5 - Consent to Act as Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If consent is not filed, the Registrar will accept a late filing with a US$25 penalty within 30 days; otherwise the corporate certificate may be suspended until compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation shareholder and directors; corporate records maintained at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the initial shareholder meeting or obtain written consent to elect directors, appoint officers, authorize share issuance, adopt corporate bylaws, and approve the first board resolution. Minutes and consents must be executed and kept in the corporate record book.
required_dossiers: Organization chart and officer acceptance letters
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the organizational documents contain omissions or procedural defects, adopt an omnibus corrective resolution at the next board meeting and file certified copies to the Registry if required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for Corporate Tax Exemption / Non-Resident Status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Tax and Revenue Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Certificate of Incorporation and a written election confirming non-resident corporate status with no income derived from business transacted within the Marshall Islands. The Tax Office will issue a tax-exempt status acknowledgment for non-resident shipping operations.
required_dossiers: Board resolution confirming non-resident status and no local business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application for exemption is contested, provide a legal opinion on source of income and vessel charter or transportation activities occurring outside RMI territorial waters; appeal within 14 days to the Tax Commissioner.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands Maritime Administrator (Office of the Maritime Administrator, International Registries, Inc. as agent)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: RMI Ship Certificate of Registry (Permanent) together with International Ship Management (ISM) Document of Compliance and International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Certificate for deep-sea Ro-Ro vehicle carrier operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Republic of the Marshall Islands Environmental Protection Authority (RMI EPA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (Vessel Environmental Compliance) – No Full EIA Report required because the activity is an internationally operating vessel with no fixed onshore facility; vessel must register for waste and discharge management with RMI EPA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with MARPOL Annex I (oil), Annex IV (sewage), Annex V (garbage), Annex VI (air emission and VOC controls); prohibition of untreated sewage discharge within 12 nm of land; no combustible or hazardous waste discharge; ballast water exchange per RMI Ballast Water Management requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate and structural load inspection approved by the RMI Maritime Administrator for Ro-Ro decks (vehicle stowage and intact stability); Domestic Workplace Health and Safety clearance for longshore and shipboard operations; cargo securing manual approval in accordance with CSS Code and RMI Marine Notice 7-041-4.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Republic of the Marshall Islands (RMI) Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Taxation Division (Majuro); official tax administration portal operated by the Ministry of Finance. Customs and maritime revenue matters are handled by the RMI Customs Service and the RMI Maritime Administrator (Office of the Maritime Administrator, administered through International Registries, Inc.).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate a Business Corporation (BC) under Title 39 of the Marshall Islands Revised Code with the RMI Registrar of Corporations, submitting Articles of Incorporation and paying the registration fee to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation. Step 2: Apply to the RMI Ministry of Finance, Revenue and Taxation Division for a Business License under the Business License Act (Title 22); the license number serves as the statutory fee/tax identifier for the non-resident BC. Step 3: If the BC will own or operate a Ro-Ro vessel, obtain a Certificate of Registry and Commercial Operating License from the RMI Maritime Administrator. Step 4: File a foreign-sales-corporation designation with the Revenue and Taxation Division to perfect the tax-exempt status; thereafter the BC files only annual license renewals and the corporate status/franking report, with no income tax return required for non-resident domestic corporations deriving no RMI-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists. Statutory elections available under MIRC Title 24 include: (i) designation as a foreign sales corporation, removing all foreign-source shipping income from RMI income tax; (ii) election to be treated as a resident domestic corporation, which would subject RMI-source earnings to the 3% branch/profit-remittance tax; and (iii) an elective hybrid-mismatch alignment for OECD BEPS Action 2 reporting. The default classification is a tax-transparent offshore entity with no RMI tax attributes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: None – No VAT, GST, or sales/use tax; the only indirect impositions are customs import duties on physical goods entering RMI and annual business license fees for commercial operations in Majuro and Ebeye.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable – no VAT/GST registration threshold exists. The indirect levy trigger is the physical importation of goods into RMI (customs duty) and the commencement of any commercial activity in RMI requiring a business license; offshore vessel operations with no RMI port calls are outside the scope of all RMI indirect taxes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Not applicable – RMI has no electronic invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based reporting mandate for tax purposes. Commercial documentation and customs declarations are filed on paper or standard electronic manifests through the RMI Customs Service and the Revenue and Taxation Division.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Structurally inapplicable because RMI imposes no VAT/GST regime and therefore operates no zero-rating or refund mechanism. International ocean carriage of vehicles by Ro-Ro vessels is classified as offshore income and is exempt from RMI income tax even without an export declaration, provided the BC has filed the foreign-sales-corporation designation and the voyage neither originates nor calls at RMI ports. If an RMI port call occurs, the freight attributable to RMI-source legs remains exempt for a non-resident domestic corporation, but cabotage licences and RMI Customs clearance are required; no statutory FX repatriation deadline applies to RMI tax purposes, though the 180-day benchmark is retained as an internal treasury/ALM standard.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: RMI Certificate of Registry and Certificate of Survey evidencing flag, ownership, and class status of the Ro-Ro vessel
Commercial Operating License issued by the RMI Maritime Administrator and, where applicable, the RMI Ministry of Finance business license for the operating entity
Original bills of lading, charter-party freight statements, and bank inward-remittance advices evidencing offshore freight earnings
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: RMI has no VAT export-refund system, so zero-rating clawback penalties are moot. Enforcement focus rests on misuse of the tax-exempt foreign-sales-corporation status: retroactive assessment at the 3% branch-tax rate on any RMI-source freight earnings plus interest; penalties under Title 22 (Business License Act) of up to USD 10,000 and suspension or revocation of the BC's business license; criminal fines and disqualification under Title 24 for wilful tax evasion; and vessel deregistration by the RMI Maritime Administrator for false tonnage, unpaid registry fees, or unlicensed cabotage.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains no central bank, establishes the U.S. dollar as the exclusive legal tender and domestic currency, and delegates monetary policy to the U.S. Federal Reserve. Financial institutions are supervised by the Banking Commissioner under the Banking Act 1989 (as amended), while the Marshall Islands Financial Services Commission and the Registrar of Business Corporations administer corporate licensing and registration. There is no Central Bank approval prerequisite for any FX transaction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Marshall Islands has no exchange control statute, no investment commission, and no foreign exchange licensing regime. Both current-account transactions (trade, freight, charterhire, interest, dividends) and capital-account movements (equity injections, shareholder loans, liquidation distributions) are freely convertible at market rates through correspondent U.S. dollar clearing. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is unrestricted and subject only to standard bank-level documentary due diligence and, where applicable, taxation at zero percent under the tax-exempt status of non-resident Business Corporations. The complete absence of local sovereign FX intervention and the use of the U.S. dollar eliminate currency convertibility risk; residual risk resides in correspondent-bank sanctions and AML screening friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export-proceeds surrender rules, mandatory conversion timelines, or prescribed repatriation percentages in Marshall Islands law. Earnings from deep-sea Ro-Ro transport services, voyage freight, demurrage, and auxiliary shipping income may be held in any currency, retained offshore, settled through on-island operational accounts, or applied to transaction costs without any obligation to deposit with, or surrender to, the Banking Commissioner or any government treasury account. Shipping entities are free to manage those proceeds as corporate treasury policy dictates, subject only to the AML/KYC requirements of their chosen banking counterparties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of Guam – Marshall Islands Branch

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. The Marshall Islands has no dedicated e-money institution or digital banking licensing framework within the Banking Act, and no offshore EMI holds a banking license or a recognized agent arrangement under the Banking Commissioner. A non-resident Business Corporation engaged in Ro-Ro shipping cannot rely on an unlicensed digital EMI as its principal treasury rail, and the Banking Commissioner would consider unauthorized payment intermediation a criminal regulatory infringement. Such EMIs may be used only for ancillary corporate expense handling in third-party jurisdictions provided the EMI is lawfully licensed where the company operates, never for the statutory capital escrow or core USD clearing function. The practical workaround is a hybrid model: a licensed Marshall Islands bank as the treasury anchor plus a niche offshore EMI approved by the bank for decentralized disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signatories of a Marshall Islands non-resident Business Corporation are not legally required to appear physically in the jurisdiction to establish a bank account. However, because the jurisdiction's banks are correspondent-dependent and inherently cautious about non-resident shipping structures, the practical onboarding requirement is a face-to-face or remote video interview with the compliance officer, coupled with an approval threshold requiring the physical presence of at least one signatory at an overseas notary for the execution certification. For the Ocean Car Carrier Ro-Ro vehicle, if the ultimate beneficial owners and executive directors are located in major shipping hubs (Singapore, Hamburg, Athens, Tokyo), the bank may accept a video interview if the corporate kit is apostilled under the Hague Convention and the beneficial ownership schedule is certified by a Marshall Islands licensed attorney. A visit to Majuro is nonetheless recommended if immediate access to high-limit USD clearing and country-specific banking products is required within thirty days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Layered beneficial ownership with discretionary trusts, nominee officers, or historical bearer share issuance patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the registered share register and directors register, full chain-of-title diagram from the registered agent to every natural-person beneficial owner, updated beneficial ownership register filed with the Registrar, apostilled trust instruments or nominee agreements, a no-issue statement from the Marshall Islands Registered Agent, and a legal opinion from resident counsel confirming the absence of bearer share instruments and compliance with the Business Corporations Act disclosure requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume wire traffic from freight and charter proceeds lacking transparent underlying voyage documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed charter party forms (BIMCO-based), bills of lading, freight and demurrage invoices, port agent disbursement accounts, bunker delivery notes, and a line-item reconciliation map from the bank statement to each specific vessel and voyage number. For intercompany charges, provide current supporting contracts and a board-approved transfer pricing policy, if cross-border related-party supplies are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large capital injection in non-base currency routed through intermediary jurisdictions without identifiable economic purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supporting source-of-funds declaration, audited previous financial statements, subscribed share certificates and subscriber ledgers, signed loan notes or equity subscription agreements, ISDA/CSA FX hedge confirmations, and a professional cash-flow memorandum showing the treasury rationale for the routing corridor (e.g., liquidity concentration at Singapore/CBEST-clearing banks).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and ship-tracking red flags on the vessel IMO number or ship manager address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Marshall Islands Registry stateless vessel certificate, continuous synopsis record (CSR), an independent negative sanctions list screening report, certified vessel tracker history showing no calls to sanctioned ports or unflagged zones, and a compliance certificate from the security officer confirming alignment with the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No recognized economic footprint in the Marshall Islands leading to shell/business-conduct recharacterization by correspondent banks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly appointed registered agent and registered office in Majuro, tax-exempt status grant under the Business Corporations Act, financial statements showing the substance of the shipping operation, commercial contracts showing general business management by the board from a recognized shipping hub, and a practical explanation of why the RMI platform (flag state neutrality, low tax, international shipping network) is both corporeal and business-driven.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and shareholder-loan injections are cleared through USD payment rails, primarily SWIFT MT103 via the funding bank to the Marshall Islands account held at Bank of Marshall Islands or an overseas clearing bank. The remittance must carry a correct ISO 20022/purpose code, e.g., 'GICT' for loans, 'DACC' or 'DISP' for direct investment equity, and reference the company name, subscription details, or loan agreement number. No Marshall Islands exchange-control endorsement is required. For U.S. dollar Fedwire and CHIPS clearing, the sending institution must perform OFAC and Specially Designated Nationals screening, and the ultimate beneficiary will be verified against the onboarding KYC file. To prevent rejection, the onboarding dossier should pre-store the last four digits of the corresponding SWIFT account, international bank account number (IBAN if applicable), and the treasury team should include the RMI registered agent's address in the beneficiary line. The funds can be used for working capital, vessel acquisition, or capital improvements once the bank matches the purpose code to the underlying corporate resolution and KYC ownership statement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for vessel operations, bunker procurement, port calls, crew wages, service dues, and ship repair are settled through: (a) SWIFT MT103 for low-value operational payments directly to suppliers and agent accounts; (b) commercial documentary letters of credit issued under UCP600 (SWIFT MT700) for high-value bunker supply, newbuilding installments, or major dry-dock invoices; and (c) bank-draft or CHIPS/Fedwire transfers for urgent disbursements where immediate credit is required. Because the Marshall Islands has no domestic electronic payment netting system, all outward USD flows are processed via overseas correspondent relationships. Trade payments to counterparties in the European Union may require the separation of bank charges under the IBAN/SEPA rules, but USD clearing remains the anchor. For settlements with Chinese/RMB-denominated suppliers, a USD-contracted LC with a Hong Kong advising bank is standard and avoids any need for on-island FX conversion. The treasury blueprint must instruct accounts payable to include in each outbound MT103 field 70 the invoice number, vessel IMO number, and definitive purpose code so that clearing banks can quickly pass OFAC filters and reduce RMA rejection risk.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forward FX contracts for USD/EUR, USD/JPY, USD/GBP, USD/SGD and USD/AUD with a licensed global bank or broker
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-deliverable currencies (USD/CNY, USD/KRW, USD/TWD) executed through a prime broker under an ISDA Master Agreement
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for USD/EUR and USD/JPY on asset-backed vessel financing to manage debt-service volatility
Plain-vanilla long-dated FX options and zero-cost collars to hedge charter income and port-fee exposures
FX products governed by the FX Global Code and cleared where appropriate through CLS (Continuous Linked Settlement) to mitigate settlement risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Report of Non-Resident Domestic Corporation (Business Corporations Act)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporations, Republic of the Marshall Islands; submitted through the AMIRA-accredited Registered Agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before the month/day anniversary of incorporation each year; the anniversary date is the absolute filing deadline and no extension is available. Standard fee tier applies to authorized share capital up to 10,000,000 shares; escalated tiers apply above that amount.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: US$50 late fee on the first day past due plus a recurring US$50-per-month delinquency charge; the Certificate of Good Standing is withheld until payment is made. Non-filing for two consecutive years authorizes administrative dissolution and strike-off, extinguishing the corporation's legal capacity to contract, litigate, or operate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Renewal or Nil-RMI-Revenue Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business License Office, Ministry of Finance, Republic of the Marshall Islands.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Licenses run on a calendar-year basis; renewal application and payment are due at the start of each calendar year, typically on or before 31 January. A RoRo operator earning exclusively foreign-source ocean freight income files a nil-revenue confirmation through its registered agent at no government cost; RMI-source gross revenue is assessed in fee bands from US$25 to US$5,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without an effective license violates the Business Licensing Act and is subject to daily administrative penalties and fines, together with refusal of RMI customs and port clearance for owned or chartered vessels until the license is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Disclosure and AML/KYC Refresh (Register Audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AMIRA-licensed Registered Agent; the Beneficial Ownership Record is made available to the RMI Competent Authority and Financial Intelligence Unit upon lawful request.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Executed concurrently with the Annual Corporate Report at each incorporation anniversary; re-executed immediately upon any share transfer, allotment, or change in ultimate beneficial owner, and in all events before the next annual validation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or misleading ownership details constitute an AML/CFT violation; the registered agent must withhold renewal processing and may file a Suspicious Transaction Report. Persistent default blocks the Certificate of Good Standing and may be referred to the Registrar for administrative action.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory zero effective tax rate; non-resident Business Corporations are outside Marshall Islands income tax jurisdiction and also benefit from the absence of capital gains tax, value-added tax, and branch remittance tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No corporate income tax return is required for non-resident Business Corporations; the sole annual filing obligation is the Annual Corporate Renewal Statement (Form AR-1) lodged through a licensed Marshall Islands Registered Agent via the online Registrar of Corporations portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The Annual Corporate Renewal Statement must be filed within ninety (90) days after the close of the corporation's fiscal year, unless extended by the Registrar of Corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered corporate name and registration number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact name shown in the Certificate of Incorporation; no alteration permitted in the renewal filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address in the Marshall Islands and name of the Registered Agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the full street address of the registered office in Majuro and the licensed agent's name; a mere P.O. Box is not acceptable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors and officers; statement of non-resident status
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all directors and officers; confirm that the corporation is a non-resident under the Income Tax Act and is not conducting business within the Republic of the Marshall Islands.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a fixed penalty of USD 300 plus a daily surcharge of USD 20 per calendar day, capped at USD 2,000; continued non-payment leads to administrative dissolution by the Registrar and loss of limited liability protection.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Republic of the Marshall Islands maintains no comprehensive double-taxation treaty network and does not issue Tax Residency Certificates for treaty-relief purposes. Outbound dividends from a non-resident BC are subject to zero domestic withholding, so no treaty protocol is required; payers should, nevertheless, retain board minutes and distribution schedules to evidence the tax-free character of the dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic withholding tax rate for both cross-border royalties and interest paid to non-residents is 0%. No treaty override is necessary. If income arises from sources within the Marshall Islands, the 3% gross revenue tax may apply to the payer instead.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable; the Marshall Islands has no statutory transfer-pricing thresholds and does not mandate Master File or Local File preparation. Non-resident BCs must, however, maintain full and accurate accounting records sufficient to substantiate that their revenue is foreign-source and that no intercompany pricing inflates local-source income.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Marshall Islands Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) apply to 'relevant activities' such as financing, leasing, distribution, and service centers. International Ro-Ro vehicle shipping is not listed as a relevant activity. Nevertheless, a non-resident BC must file an annual Economic Substance Declaration with its Registered Agent confirming that no relevant activity is conducted in the Marshall Islands, and maintain records refuting any de facto local management and control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting vessel loading, crew payroll, office operations, or managing voyage contracts from within the Marshall Islands while claiming non-resident foreign-source exemption; or filing a nil income declaration while generating revenue through a Majuro-based agency.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Assessment of the 3% gross revenue tax retroactively on all Marshall Islands-sourced revenue, interest at 1% per month, and penalties of up to 150% of the assessed tax; flagrant non-compliance triggers strike-off by the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties; intentional under-reporting may result in travel bans and up to seven years' imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the BC as a hollow vehicle to conceal beneficial ownership, evade foreign taxes, or misrepresent the Majuro registered office as an operational hub in commercial documentation to third parties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The High Court may order judicial dissolution, asset attachment, and a civil penalty of USD 5,000–50,000 under the Business Corporations Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil exposes directors and shareholders to civil restitution to creditors; the court may also prohibit a director from acting in a managerial capacity for five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain a beneficial ownership register, failure to appoint a local anti-money-laundering officer, or omission of the annual Economic Substance Declaration despite qualifying as a relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary fine of USD 25,000 and revocation of the Registered Agent's license; the entity may be struck off and any local assets escheated to the Republic.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal fines of USD 10,000 and imprisonment of up to two years for knowingly submitting a false declaration.
